steps.headline: PDFs get the same zoom bar as pictures, in the same corner.
steps.changed: Minus, the current size, plus, and the magnifier — identical to the picture viewer, so the control does not move when you switch between a photo and a document. 100% means the size a PDF has always opened at.
steps.measured: Pages were fixed at one size with no control of any kind
steps.notice: Nothing about how a PDF first opens has changed: same size, same position, same scrolling. The bar is simply there now.
steps.risk: Ctrl+F opens the Find bar in this corner too, and on a PDF searching is a real thing to do. The zoom bar steps down while the Find bar is open, the same as it does on a picture.

steps.path: Session files → any PDF → zoom in twice
steps.headline: Zooming a PDF redraws the page bigger and SHARPER, rather than blowing up a blurry copy.
steps.changed: The page is re-rendered at the new size by the PDF engine itself, so the text is crisp at 200% and at 400%. Enlarging a picture cannot do this — a photo just gets bigger pixels.
steps.measured: 6pt lines that are a grey smear at 100% are ordinary readable text at 200%
steps.notice: The page becomes wider than the pane, so it scrolls sideways as well as down. Zoom snaps to set sizes (100, 150, 200, 400…) rather than sliding.
steps.risk: Redrawing is not instant on a big document — expect a brief moment before the page sharpens. Very large pages stop at a size limit, and the plus button then explains why it is greyed out rather than producing a blank page.

steps.path: Session files → any PDF → magnifier on
steps.headline: The magnifier works on PDF pages, for reading fine print without leaving your place.
steps.changed: Same lens and same crosshair as on a picture. It reads whatever page is under the cursor, so it keeps working as you scroll through the document, and it shows nothing in the gaps between pages.
steps.measured: The 6pt line under the lens reads 'legible only when enlarged'; the same line outside it does not
steps.notice: The lens is instant — it magnifies the page as already drawn, with no redraw and no pause. That also means it is slightly softer than zooming in properly.
steps.risk: For a long read, zooming is better than the lens: zoom redraws sharp, the lens only enlarges what is on screen.
